description.value: A cross-sectional fMRI study investigated associations of insulin resistance, anthropometric measurements, and behavioral factors with food reward-related brain activation in overweight or obese individuals at risk of type 2 diabetes.

spans.text: In this clinical study, we investigated the respective contribution of insulin resistance, anthropometric measurements, and behavioral factors to brain reward activation in response to visual stimuli.

value: brain reward signaling would be primarily associated with insulin resistance rather than weight status or behavioral variables

spans.text: Given the evidence so far, it was our hypothesis that brain reward signaling would be primarily associated with insulin resistance rather than weight status or behavioral variables.

value: Food compared with nonfood brain activation was positively associated with HOMA-IR in the right and left insula and the right cingulate gyrus.

Activation in the right nucleus accumbens was significantly associated with HOMA-IR, and activation in the left nucleus accumbens remained significantly associated with HOMA-IR after correction for BMI and age.

Food reward-related brain activation was positively associated with insulin resistance during the anticipation of food reward, specifically in the nucleus accumbens, left and right insula, and right cingulate gyrus, independently of BMI.

value: Food compared with nonfood brain activation was positively related to TFEQ factor 2 (emotional eating and disinhibition) in the right supramarginal gyrus.
Emotional eating and disinhibition were positively associated with brain reactivity to food cues in the supramarginal gyrus, which may lead to changes in food preference and hyperphagia.
